### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **76** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**75** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c4a73be6be58671e8f69007e5e615646aa172d91`.

⛔ **17** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`, `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 41 pages)`
- **19** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c4a73be6be58671e8f69007e5e615646aa172d91` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cd528447a15a6787b83aa8fa7abf2bb26bd49379` — the merge of head `f8d04024eb16e19ad64f89015e7dc3fb54c1f9fd` into base `c4a73be6be58671e8f69007e5e615646aa172d91`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cd528447a15a6787b83aa8fa7abf2bb26bd49379 && git checkout cd528447a15a6787b83aa8fa7abf2bb26bd49379
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c4a73be6be58671e8f69007e5e615646aa172d91 f8d04024eb16e19ad64f89015e7dc3fb54c1f9fd && git checkout -B drift-repro c4a73be6be58671e8f69007e5e615646aa172d91 && git merge --no-ff f8d04024eb16e19ad64f89015e7dc3fb54c1f9fd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c4a73be6be58671e8f69007e5e615646aa172d91
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c4a73be6be58671e8f69007e5e615646aa172d91` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Seat check

**L1: ACCEPT** (L1-a, for area d7-D) at head `98693f501d749399a2b395177b10076f7ff37fd9`, read 2026-11-20T05:28Z. The contract (L2) review at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER is owed and is being run by d7-D as an isolated reviewer. This ACCEPT does not replace it.

### Shape and declarations

- Draft, base `main`, 15 files, +1942/−13 (under the 3,000-line seat line). `Fixes #35571` is the only closing keyword. It fits: the card's scope list is fully covered (brand, factory and guard; the door option; the inner read's description; the case-set; the `ISharingService` / `ISecurityService` prose). The two deferrals in the acceptance notes are outside that list: the driver declaration, proposed for step 2 as `DriverCapabilities.fixedReadLeaves`, and the write-form-on-read-verb seam case.
- `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none` sit at line start in the body and the changeset. `none` is right: no operator, CEL function or lint vocabulary spells the leaf, and `check:authorable-surface` is unmoved.
- **Changeset level.** `'@objectstack/spec': patch` beside `none` is ruling A, and `check-changeset-no-major` refuses `minor` there. The body drives both levels with `--event`, and CI `Check Changeset` is `success`.
- **No runtime change.** I read every changed code path for this. The one edit to an existing path is `admitsEngineLeaf`. For every existing caller it answers exactly what `op === '$in' && admitReadableIds && isReadableIds(comparand)` did:
  - `options === undefined` → `false`;
  - `admitReadableIds === true && isReadableIds` → `true`;
  - the new arm is reached only with `admitFixedReadLeaves` set, and no caller in the tree passes it (`git grep` over `packages/**` outside spec: the engine door and the three analytics call sites pass `{ admitReadableIds: true }` only).
  - The recursion at lines 1080/1085/1091 hands the same `options` down.

### Code

- **`isSharedRecordIds`** is strict and ordered right. It checks:
  - exactly one own symbol, which must be the brand, holding `true`;
  - the value is frozen;
  - the closed key set;
  - non-empty `object` and `recipient`;
  - `accessLevels`, when it is an own key, is a non-empty frozen list of non-empty strings.

  `brand()` defines the symbol non-enumerable, non-writable and non-configurable before `Object.freeze`, so spreads, JSON and `structuredClone` all drop it. That is the same device as `ReadableIds`.
- **`innerRead`** answers a fresh frozen description every call: `sys_record_share` / `record_id`, with `object_name`, `recipient_type = 'user'` and `recipient_id` under `equals`. The write form adds `access_level` under `memberOf`, and `tenantScope` is the literal `'none'`. The literal type makes a later leaf that rules otherwise widen the type and force every evaluator to answer it. That matches ADR-0155 D2 and ① A as the ADR text reads.
- **`fixed-read-leaf.ts`.** The dispatch table is private, the guards are disjoint by the one-symbol rule, and `isFixedReadLeaf(value, brands)` treats a non-list `brands` as naming nothing (2f90e449). The evaluator duties in the module doc are the ADR's D2/D4 list: the blank-id guard, system authority, no inner tenant scope, set semantics, the same datasource, and no `EXISTS`, correlated form or join. The NOT IN / NULL reasoning is correct SQL.
- **Contract prose** (`sharing-service.ts`, `security-service.ts`). I checked it against ADR-0155 D4 sentence by sentence:
  - the recipient rule (the context's user, its delegator under ADR-0090 D10, or a system context; otherwise `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500);
  - the by-name class, including plugin-audit's record-view opt-in, which gets R1 at boot with the seam's refusal behind it, with no exemption for a handler that skips system reads;
  - the no-object boundary ("is not run on the share arm … this paragraph is the telling").

  All of it is stated as holding "from plugin-sharing's switch on", so nothing claims today's behaviour has changed. "At most 5,000 grants per read" matches `sharing-service.ts:787` (`limit: 5000`).

### Case-set

I recomputed every `matches` case's expected rows by hand from the fixtures, and each one holds:

- read u1 → `d1 d2 d7 d8`. g4 is u2's, g5 is another object, g6 is a group, and g9/g10 are blank.
- write u1 (edit, full) → `d2 d7 d8`. write u1 (full) → `d7`.
- `readScope(u1)` → `+d3`. `readScope(u3)` → `d9`.
- `label: keep` → drops d7.
- `$not` → `d3 d4 d5 d6 d9`. This is the case that witnesses the blank-id guard through g9.
- Tenant `org_a` → `d1 d2 d7`. g7, stamped `org_b`, still counts, and the outer wall drops d8.
- The note scope → `n1 n2`. n3's doc is neither owned nor shared, and n4 is NULL.

The D-0 list case (`holdsLeaf: false`) is today's `grantedRecordIds` reading of the same fixture. The 21 seam cases match D1's position and verb list, ③ A (the write form on a predicate update only, delete refused), and D4's recipient rule, including the delegated intersection and the third-identity refusal.

### Tests and controls

- **Refusal pins.** Every refusal pin asserts the envelope (`INVALID_FILTER` / 400 via `envelopeOf`, plus the message head and the path), never a bare throw. The door test walks `undefined`, `{}`, `[]`, `admitReadableIds` only and `admitFixedReadLeaves: true`. JSON, `structuredClone`, the plain-object spelling, `$nin` and `parseFilterAST` are each pinned 400 even for the admitting caller.
- **Positive controls.** The conformance test's wrong readings (blank guard missing, inner read walled, the leaf read as no restriction, each fixed predicate unfixed, levels ignored, restated or joined) and the four forgetful seam judges are positive controls built into the suite, so the case-set is shown to discriminate, not only to pass.
- **Ablation.** The door brand check was mutated, and the reading was 1 failed / 29 passed. The failing test is the no-brand walk above. The file was restored blob-equal.
- **The reconcile test** reads `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/sys-record-share.object.ts` (the relative path resolves from `src/data`). It is registered in `vitest.repo-tests.json`, which is the right project for a cross-package read.

### Gates

- CI at `98693f50`: 69 check runs, 58 `success` and 11 `skipped`, none red. Among them are `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` with all 10 shards, `Test UI` with all 16 shards, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `PR-body guards`.
- The local sweep was read at `d475dae3` (91/91 exit 0). The delta to the head is the one anchor JSON, and CI covers `check:adr-anchors` at the head.

### Recorded corrections to the PR body (not patched, per the body-signature trap)

- "No ADR anchor file for the new module … It is left to the seat" is **stale**. `98693f50` adds `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__spec__src__data__shared-record-ids.ts.json`, which names ADR-0139 and ADR-0155 and carries an invariant matching the module. One anchor for the leaf module follows the `readable-ids.ts` precedent, where the conformance module carries none. This line supersedes the body's.
- The Verification block's local readings are at `d475dae3`, not the head. The head adds only that JSON file, so the readings stand for code.

### Nits (no change owed for this ACCEPT)

1. **Changeset prose.** "read from `sys_record_share` at most 5,000 grants at a time" reads as if the read pages. It is one read capped at 5,000 (`limit: 5000`), as the sharing-service doc says ("at most 5,000 grants per read"). If the changeset is touched again, use the same wording.
2. **`SharedRecordIds.write` and a sparse level list.** `accessLevels.every(isNonEmptyString)` skips holes, so `write('a', 'u', [, 'edit'])` builds a leaf whose `[...accessLevels]` copy holds `undefined`. Its own guard then refuses it: a 400 at the door and a `TypeError` from `innerRead`. It fails closed, and only the producer can hit it. A length-and-index check in the factory would refuse it at construction instead.

### Review routing

The L2 is owed at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER (a published `packages/spec/src/**` surface with `Clause-②: yes`), and d7-D runs it on this head. Before handing the PR on, the area runs `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35739` to read the tier. A governed or Tier-H answer sends it to the seat for the maintainer's approval.

- **`packages/spec/src/data/fixed-read-leaf-conformance.ts`: holds, with N3 and N4.** All 13 evaluator cases were recomputed by hand from the fixture's 9 docs, 10 grant rows and 4 notes, and each expected set is right: G(doc, u1) is d1, d2, d7, d8; the write form is d2, d7, d8; `$not` answers d3, d4, d5, d6, d9; the tenant-walled outer read under org_a still answers d1, d2, d7; the nested case answers n1, n2. The 21 seam cases agree with D1's position rule, ③'s verb rule and D4's recipient rule on its four cases (the context's user, its delegator, a system context, any other recipient refused).
